# Filament cost calculator

> Calculate exact 3D print material cost from slicer weight, net spool weight, and spool price, with optional printer electricity cost and a filament density reference table.

## Calculator
- [Open the calculator](https://filamentcostcalculator.com/): With electricity: a 120 g print (+10% extra) on a $25/kg spool running 5 hours at 120 W ($0.16/kWh) costs $3.30 material + $0.10 power = $3.40. Material only: a $20, 1,000 g spool and a 50 g print cost $1.10 when 10% extra material is included ($0.0200/g).

## Guide
- [How to calculate the filament cost of a 3D print](https://filamentcostcalculator.com/guide/): step-by-step measuring, common mistakes, and ordering checklist.

## Formula and method
Cost per gram = spool price / net spool weight; Material cost = cost per gram × print weight × (1 + extra / 100); Electricity cost = (printer watts / 1000) × print hours × rate per kWh.

Divide spool price by net filament weight in grams to obtain unit cost per gram. Multiply by slicer material weight adjusted for any uncounted waste percentage. When electricity is enabled, multiply average wattage in kilowatts by print duration and your local energy tariff.

## Limits
Net spool weight means plastic only—exclude the empty reel weight (often 180 g to 260 g). Changing the currency label does not convert exchange rates. Printer depreciation, failed jobs, post-processing, and labor are separate from material and power cost.

## Common 1.75 mm filament densities and approximate length per 1 kg spool

Slicers report both grams and meters; density explains why 1 kg of ABS gives more linear meters than 1 kg of PETG.

| Material | Typical density | Approx. length per 1 kg (1.75 mm) | Typical spool price (1 kg) | Common use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PLA | 1.24 g/cm³ | ~335 m (1,100 ft) | $15–$25 | General prototypes, models |
| PETG | 1.27 g/cm³ | ~327 m (1,073 ft) | $18–$28 | Functional, moisture-resistant parts |
| ABS | 1.04 g/cm³ | ~400 m (1,312 ft) | $18–$30 | Heat-resistant enclosures (enclosed printer) |
| ASA | 1.07 g/cm³ | ~388 m (1,273 ft) | $22–$35 | Outdoor UV-resistant parts |
| TPU (95A) | 1.21 g/cm³ | ~344 m (1,129 ft) | $25–$40 | Flexible bumpers, gaskets |
| Nylon (PA) | 1.14 g/cm³ | ~365 m (1,197 ft) | $35–$65 | High-strength mechanical parts |

## Step by step
1. Slice the model with your real layer height, infill, walls, supports, and brim or raft settings, then record the total filament weight in grams.
2. Check the spool price (including shipping if you track landed cost) and the net filament weight printed on the box, typically 1,000 g or 750 g.
3. Add a small extra percentage only for waste not already in the slicer total, such as purge towers, color swaps, or expected test prints.
4. Optionally enable the electricity section and enter print duration in hours, average printer wattage, and your local kWh rate.

## Common mistakes
- Weighing a full spool on a kitchen scale without subtracting the empty reel (which often weighs 180 g to 260 g).
- Double-counting support and purge weight when your slicer already includes them in the gram total.
- Treating raw filament cost as a commercial selling price. Machine depreciation, failed prints, post-processing, and labor are separate business costs.
- Assuming different filament materials have the same cost per meter. Density varies from ~1.04 g/cm³ (ABS) to ~1.27 g/cm³ (PETG).

## Worked examples
### Example 1
Material only: a $20, 1,000 g spool and a 50 g print cost $1.10 when 10% extra material is included ($0.0200/g).

### Example 2
With electricity: a 120 g print (+10% extra) on a $25/kg spool running 5 hours at 120 W ($0.16/kWh) costs $3.30 material + $0.10 power = $3.40.
